newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO/Bund spread seen testing 20 bp support.
newsitem.headline: OLO/Bund spread seen testing 20 bp support.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds outperformed Bunds in Monday afternoon trading, pushing their yield premium over Bunds to 20 bp at the close, from 22 Friday.
The were boosted by good demand for the new 2007 OLO at today's monthly auction, a trend towards convergence trades in Europe and confidence in the 1997 budget talks.
Dealers said that if the trend for convergence trades following the ECOFIN meeting in Dublin this weekend continued, the spread could test the 20 bp level and fall below it.
The 2006 benchmark bond closed with a yield of 6.39 percent, up three bp.
Dealers welcomed the 25 billion francs allotted in the new March 2007 benchmark at today's monthly auction.
"The bond will probably be on auction in the coming months too, so that we will soon get the necessary 50 to 60 billion francs worth of liquidity to make it a benchmark," one dealer said.
Money market yields and the franc closed virtually unchanged.
Dealers said that one week before the presentation of the 1997 budget to parliament, the market had confidence the government would manage to cut the deficit to below three percent of GDP.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
